resources.string: Logs
Privacy
Logs are used only to help diagnose problems such as failed connections.
Logs stay on this phone by default, covering about the last 24 hours. They are uploaded only after you choose “Upload online and show QR code” and agree.

OpenXPlay is a fully open-source, free project, so the log server depends on which spare computing resources the author has, and its address may change. Uploaded logs currently pass through Cloudflare (not stored there) and are stored on a free service provided by Instabox, possibly in an AWS data center in the United States.

Logs uploaded from this app are linked automatically through a random ID. The ID is not derived from your iPhone, car or phone hardware, and a new one is created if you uninstall the app or clear its data.

Passwords, keys, phone numbers, names, messages and precise location are replaced before anything is stored. Technical details such as the phone model, Android version, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi addresses, IP addresses and Wi-Fi network names are kept to locate problems.

You can view the receipt for 48 hours after uploading. Uploaded logs cannot be downloaded publicly; they are kept for at most 72 hours and then permanently deleted from our server automatically. To have one deleted sooner, send its log ID to support@openxplay.org.

If you would rather not upload to these servers, choose “Save to a file on this phone”: the ZIP file is written only to the place you pick and the app does not use the network. Then send it to the author in a private message in the community groups or by email to support@openxplay.org.

The logs will be uploaded to logs.openxplay.org, used only to help diagnose problems such as failed connections, and cannot be downloaded publicly.

You can view the receipt for 48 hours after uploading. Logs are kept for at most 72 hours, then permanently deleted from our server automatically. Logs uploaded from this app are linked by a random ID.
If you mind, choose “Save to a file on this phone” instead: the app does not use the network, and you can send the file to the author privately.
